status_quo.label: Status quo: append loads, weekly look, exact names, keyword rules, ingestion dates

model_alone.label: Model alone: every article to the large model, its label accepted

cheap_model_alone.label: Small model alone: every article to the small model, its label accepted

platform.label: Platform: idempotent loads, monitors, backfills, weighted resolution, cascade, evidence dates

no_renormalise.label: Platform without renormalised weights (a missing field scores zero)

no_rules.label: Platform without the rule tier (every article starts at the small model)

no_review.label: Platform without the review queue (low-confidence labels accepted)

missing_as_zero.label: Platform without backfills, counting a missing week of job posts as zero

no_dark_signal.label: Platform without the jobs-feed shutdown signal

gates.why: A wrong merge mixes two companies' funding and partners; it is worse than a missed one.
Duplicates that slip through split a company's signals and clutter search.
Relationship types drive PoC tracking and recommendations; a mislabelled acquisition is visible to customers.
Classifying the backlog and the daily inflow must stay within budget.
A feed that stops must alert within about a day and a half, not when a customer notices.
Signals are sorted and alerted by date; a funding round dated by ingestion is weeks late.
Recommending a startup that was acquired or shut down a week or more ago embarrasses the customer.
